column1: # Words Arabic speakers routinely write in the Arabic script but which are NOT
# phonetically derivable from the Arabizi phonetic rules: English spelling says
# little about English sound, and Arabic writes long vowels the rules cannot
# guess, so "mobile" would come out مبلة and "phone" بهنة. Typed on the Arabic
# phonetic layout, the English spelling on the left commits the Arabic on the
# Kept short on purpose. A word is here only if the Arabic script is how it is
# normally written in Arabic text (موبايل, كمبيوتر, دكتور); a word Arabic has its
# own word for (school مدرسة, ticket تذكرة) is not a loanword and stays out, and
# anything people write in Latin letters even mid-Arabic-sentence belongs in the
# English-words setting instead, not here. Spellings follow the ar_full
# frequency list; where Egypt and the Gulf differ, both are offered (جروب,
# قروب). It is a draft and wants an Arabic speaker's review.
# Format: spelling<TAB>arabic   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
